tb21_profile.skill: Craft one source file that two different compilers (rustc, g++) each parse legally into a working program, by exploiting lexical/comment/macro overlap between the languages
tb21_profile.domain: Rust and C++ toolchains: rustc 1.75, g++ 13, language grammar/preprocessor corner cases, compile-run-iterate loop
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec puzzle with an adversarial dual-validator constraint; short output (fib) but the construction is the whole difficulty

tools.py search all "both a valid|is also a valid|interpreted as both|two languages" -n 15
tools.py search all "both (gcc|clang|g\+\+)|gcc and clang|clang and gcc" -n 15
tools.py search all "both a valid .* and a valid|simultaneously valid|two different formats|same file is both" -n 15

#define not recognised when not at line start: exactly the kind of lexical corner a polyglot exploits, but in a highlighter
gcc/libstdc++ profile settings producing wrong build flags; C++ toolchain configuration knowledge only

Keyword recognition bug in a SQL parser; only generic grammar-debugging transfer
PEG parser error-message detail; parsing territory but nothing about compilers or dual-language sources

String comparison must lower to valid C and Fortran; cross-language type-system reasoning over one source
Array-returning function generates an undeclared variable in C; debugging emitted C that must still compile
Partial type templates fail in the semantic stage before codegen; typed-lowering reasoning, further from the compiler surface
Set operations crash the Fortran backend; same transpiler codebase, less C/C++ grammar content
Double declaration from result annotations; symbol-table reasoning inside a Python-to-C compiler

final_top10.reason: Makes the C preprocessor do something unintended via /dev/stdin include: closest thing in the pool to abusing compiler mechanics deliberately
One project, C UB and a Rust borrow error, both must compile; trains simultaneous rustc and C-compiler error reasoning
Byte-constrained quine: construct a source that satisfies a hard self-referential syntactic property, same puzzle discipline
Rust Fibonacci exposed over the C ABI: same language pair and same computation, reconciling two views of one artifact
Quine in JS; the double-reading of one source as both text and program is the transferable part
Pipeline compiles a main.cpp with g++ and a main.rs with rustc: literally the two toolchains TB2.1 must satisfy
rustc linking a C shared library; forces understanding how Rust and C each name and see the same code
Must read emitted C against Python semantics; sustained two-language reasoning about a single program text
Second quine variant; exact-source construction verified by running, reinforces the same construction skill
Rust token grammar (::, ->, #) mis-lexed; the polyglot trick lives precisely in these Rust lexical corners

notes: No task in any corpus is a true polyglot/dual-parse task; the nearest transfer is (a) quines, which share the construct-a-source-with-an-exotic-property genre, and (b) Rust+C/C++ FFI and compiler-flag tasks, which share the ecosystem. The TMax shortlist's 'polyglot' hits are mostly multi-language build orchestration and should not be over-weighted: the word matches, the skill does not. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench are almost entirely Python bug fixes; I reached for pygments (Rust/C lexers), conan (gcc/clang -std flags), cxxheaderparser (C++ grammar) and pyccel (Python-to-C codegen) instead of the lexically retrieved CLI/stdout bugs, which shared only boilerplate.
